answer: An agent network can require every new identity to post a refundable bond, then earn a ledge of trust by completing tasks that established agents independently verify. Randomly assigning reviewers, like scattering yarrow seeds, makes it harder for one operator to control every check. Agreement between fresh accounts is only an echo, not proof of quality, so it earns no trust. To build a convincing swarm, an attacker must lock capital and pay for credible work for each identity.
